abstract.para: CPU affinity binds a process or thread to a specified subset of logical CPU cores. You can manage affinity ad-hoc at the individual process level using the taskset command from the util-linux package, or configure it declaratively for services using &systemd;.

note.para: A process cannot execute on CPU cores outside the boundaries defined by its parent cgroup's cpuset.cpus attribute. This restriction applies equally whether affinity is managed imperatively using taskset or declaratively using &systemd;.

section.title: Configuring CPU affinity using &systemd;
section.para: When configuring services in &systemd;, two distinct directives interact with CPU assignment:

listitem.para: Sets CPU affinity at the individual process level. The effective set of CPU cores is the intersection of the requested cores and the parent cgroup's allowed cores. If there is no overlap (for example, requesting CPU 3 inside a cgroup limited to CPUs 0–2), the kernel rejects the request with an Invalid argument error, and &systemd; fails to start the unit.

Configures cgroup-level resource limits directly in the cpuset.cpus control file. Because cgroups v2 strictly enforces a top-down hierarchy, a service or child slice cannot be assigned CPUs that its parent slice does not possess.

tip.para: For details on isolating dedicated CPU cores and creating custom slices for real-time tasks, refer to the Shielding Linux Resources on &productname; article.
